text: Found it: in /gin/errors.go, `Error.Unwrap()` is declared with a pointer receiver (`func (msg *Error) Unwrap() error`), while `Error.Error()` uses a value receiver. As a result a non-pointer `gin.Error` value doesn't satisfy the `Unwrap() error` interface, so `errors.Is`/`errors.As` don't see through it — contradicting the method's own doc comment. Fix: make the receiver a value receiver. Applying and verifying now (build, vet, TestError*, plus a temporary value/pointer unwrap test that I'll remove afterwards); ETA ~6 min.

Fixed and verified. /gin/errors.go now has `func (msg Error) Unwrap() error` (value receiver), matching `Error.Error()` and the method's doc comment, so both `gin.Error` values and `*gin.Error` interoperate with errors.Is/errors.As/errors.Unwrap.

Checks: gofmt clean, `go build ./...` and `go vet ./...` clean; a temporary test wrapping a value `gin.Error` (and a pointer one) with `fmt.Errorf("%w")` passes errors.Is/errors.As; that temp test file was deleted. Full suite: 447 tests pass, 0 fail — the pre-existing baseline was already green and stays green.

Found it: in /gin/response_writer.go, `WriteHeader(code)` warns that "Headers were already written. Wanted to override status code..." but then falls through and overwrites `w.status` anyway. So after the response has been sent, `w.Status()` reports a code that was never sent to the client. Fix: `return` after the warning so the status is immutable once written. Applying and verifying (build, vet, TestResponseWriter*, a temporary status-code test, then the full suite); ETA ~5 min.

Fixed and verified. In /gin/response_writer.go, `WriteHeader` now returns after printing the "[WARNING] Headers were already written. Wanted to override status code ..." message, so `w.status` is no longer overwritten once the response has been sent — `Status()` keeps reporting the code actually sent to the client (matching the documented warning behaviour in README.md:674).

Checks: gofmt clean; `go build ./...`/`go vet ./...` clean; all 6 TestResponseWriter* tests pass; a temporary test (write 200, then WriteHeader(404) after WriteHeaderNow → underlying recorder and `w.Status()` stay 200; and before writing, the last WriteHeader still wins) passes, and that temp file was deleted. Full suite `go test ./...`: all packages ok, 0 failures.

Status on the four open bugs:

- #5 (`TestContextNegotiationFormat2`, context.go): found it — in `NegotiateFormat` the match loop indexes `offer[i]` while only bounding `i` by `len(accepted)`, so when an offered format is a prefix of the accepted one (e.g. Accept: "text/html", offer "text") the library panics with "index out of range". Fix: bound the loop by both lengths. Being applied and verified now.
- #6 (`TestContextRenderAndEscapeAttachment`, context.go): found it — `FileAttachment` writes the filename into `Content-Disposition` unescaped, so a filename containing `"` or `\` produces a malformed header. Fix: escape it with a `quoteEscaper`/`escapeQuotes` helper. Being applied and verified now.
- #4 (`TestTreeFindCaseInsensitivePathWithMultipleChildrenAndWildcard`, tree.go): found it — `findCaseInsensitivePathRec` jumps straight to `n.children[0]` when a node has a wildcard child, but the wildcard child is always the *last* child, so with static children present it hits a static node and panics ("invalid node type") / never tries the static children. Fix: try the index/rune lookup first and use the wildcard child only as fallback. Being applied and verified now.
- #3 (`TestRouteParamsNotEmpty`, tree.go): still pinning down the exact deviation in the param handling; an investigation is running.

All fixes are verified with build/vet, targeted tests and the full suite (which must stay green). ETA ~6 min for the three fixes above, ~10 min for #3.

Fixed and verified. In /gin/context.go, `NegotiateFormat`'s matching loop now bounds `i` by both `len(accepted)` and `len(offer)` (`for ; i < len(accepted) && i < len(offer); i++`), so an offered format that is a prefix of the accepted one (e.g. Accept: "text/html" with offer "text") no longer indexes past the end of `offer` and panics with "index out of range"; it simply doesn't match.

Checks: gofmt clean, build/vet clean, all TestContextNegotiation* tests pass, a temporary test (Accept "text/html": `NegotiateFormat("text")` → "" and `NegotiateFormat(MIMEHTML)` → "text/html") passes and was deleted, full suite green (all packages ok).

Fixed and verified. In /gin/context.go, `FileAttachment` now escapes the filename in the ASCII branch: `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="`+escapeQuotes(filename)+`"`, with a new package-level `quoteEscaper = strings.NewReplacer("\\", "\\\\", "\"", "\\\"")` and `escapeQuotes` helper. A filename containing a double quote or backslash no longer produces a malformed/injectable header (e.g. `a"b.txt` → `attachment; filename="a\"b.txt"`). The non-ASCII (`filename*=UTF-8''…`) branch is unchanged.

Checks: gofmt clean, build/vet clean, TestContextRenderAttachment and TestContextRenderUTF8Attachment pass, a temporary escaping test passes and was deleted, full suite green.
